**Starts** once #54 is merged.

## Why

The coordinator can't read the whole itinerary of a long trip. #54 built `read_itinerary`, and measured a whole read of a 14-day trip at about 38,000 tokens. Claude Code returns at most 25,000 tokens of a tool result, so the tool refuses the read with an error. Technical spec 5.2 has the coordinator read the whole itinerary at the start of each session, after a resume, and to answer "what's left to decide?". On a trip longer than about a week, it gets the error in all three. This spike finds out how to handle that: read less in those cases, put less in a whole read, or allow a larger reply.

## Design

- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), section 2.1 (`read_itinerary`, its size limit, and the measurement).
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), sections 5.2 (when the coordinator reads the whole itinerary) and 7.2 (what the coordinator sees).

## What #54 found

**The trip measured.** A 14-day loop from Las Vegas with 8 stays, five stops a day, three candidates for each stop and stay, and a second set of three for about one in four of them. That's 312 candidates. It's `src/domain/fourteen-day-example.fake.ts`. Its places are made up, but each has the length of a real Google name, type, and address. Tool design 2.1 had estimated a trip like this at about 300 candidates and 20,000 tokens.

**The size of its whole read.** 72,264 characters, in 683 lines. The API counts it as 38,271 tokens for `claude-opus-5-5`, the coordinator's model. That's 1.89 characters a token. Plain English, the first 20,000 characters of DEVELOPMENT.md, came to 2.9. Tokens were counted by sending the text through the Agent SDK and taking the input tokens less those of a one-word prompt, since the plan token has no API key for the token count endpoint.

**Where the tokens go.** Measured on an earlier version of the read, at 75,613 characters:

- The 312 candidate lines were 44,832 characters and 23,183 tokens, about 60% of the read. Each gives its set, name, place ID, short line, and visit and detour times. The selected one also gives its rationale.
- Everything else was 30,800 characters and 16,177 tokens: stays, days, legs, schedules, stop lines, and check results.
- The read holds 496 IDs, such as `place_k7m2x9qa`. IDs and short lines are what make the read cost more tokens than prose.

**Scoped reads.** Each day of the trip reads at 5,202 characters at most. A stay read gives every candidate's full details, so a 3-night stay is 28,104 characters, and a 1-night stay about 12,000. A stay of 5 nights or more at this density would be refused too.

**What the tool does now.** It refuses any reply over 40,000 characters, about 21,000 tokens at 1.89, with "Can't read the itinerary: it's too large to return. Read one day, stay, or stop at a time instead." At this density, a whole read fits a trip of about a week.

**What Claude Code does over the limit.** It saves a tool result over 25,000 tokens to a file, and gives the model only the file's path and a short preview. The coordinator has no Read tool, so for it the result is cut off, with nothing to say so. 25,000 is Claude Code's default for MCP tools, and nothing in Claude Code 2.1.301, which SDK 0.3.301 ships, treats in-process servers differently.

**Every read stays in context.** A 38,000-token read at the start of each session uses that much of every later turn's input, and goes out of date with the next change.

## A realistic whole read

[Research doc: making a whole itinerary read smaller](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/research/itinerary-read-size.md) (`research/itinerary-read-size.md`) measures a realistic 14-day read, what each change to the format would save, and what each costs the coordinator. Today's whole read of a busy trip is 66,260 characters and 34,498 tokens. The proposal in its section 5 brings it to 27,582 characters and 15,291 tokens. `research/itinerary-read-size/slim-read-proposed.txt` shows the proposed format, on the same trip with its last stay still undecided.

## Open questions

- ~~In each of the three cases in technical spec 5.2, what does the coordinator need from the read? Example: "what's left to decide?" needs empty and proposed stops and lodging, and open warnings, not every candidate.~~ Settled on 2026-10-26, in chat: the start of a session needs the open warnings, the forecast notes, and the trip as it stands. A resume needs the same, and also has to spot what the conversation never heard about (#147 asks whether to add a list of changes). "What's left to decide?" needs the empty and proposed items, the open warnings, and the approvals. None needs every candidate. Research doc section 2.1.
- ~~Can a whole read carry less, and still do its job? Example: each stop's selected place and a count of its other candidates, leaving the full list to a read of the stay or stop. Tool design 2.1 says a whole read gives every candidate, so this would change it.~~ Settled on 2026-10-26, in chat: yes. The whole read gives each picked place with its town, counts the other candidates by set, and leaves out the rationale, weather text, and tier rules, which the itinerary view shows. Research doc section 5.
- ~~Should there be a new scope for a summary, such as one for what's left to decide?~~ Settled on 2026-10-26, in chat: no. The slimmer whole read is about 15,000 tokens on a busy 14-day trip, and answers "what's left to decide?" itself.
- ~~Could the coordinator read a long trip a stay at a time in those cases, with only instructions changing?~~ Settled on 2026-10-26, in chat: no. It would lose the parts that only a whole read shows, and the slimmer whole read fits.
- ~~Should the limit go up? Claude Code has a setting for it, `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS`. Check whether it applies to an in-process server through the Agent SDK, and what a larger read costs in context on every later turn. Tool design 2.1 now says raising the limit isn't the fix, so a yes changes it.~~ Settled on 2026-10-26, in chat: no. The slimmer whole read fits under 25,000 tokens, and under the tool's 40,000-character limit, so neither changes. Research doc section 10.
- ~~Can the format itself cost fewer tokens, such as fewer IDs, without making a read harder for the coordinator to act on?~~ Settled on 2026-10-26, in chat: yes, in the ways research doc section 5 lists. Fewer IDs, no: the coordinator needs each one to act on its item (section 13).
- ~~Whichever way is chosen has to reach the parts that only a whole read shows today, raised in PR #128's review (finding comment-4364853766). The check results whose subject is the itinerary, such as the trip length ("The trip is 10 days, and the brief asks for 11."), are in no day, stay, or stop read, since each of those filters results by subject (`checkLines` in `src/tools/itinerary-lines.ts`). Nor are the start and end places, the dates, or the rejected places. So on a trip whose whole read is refused, the coordinator never sees them, and the start-of-session bullet on open warnings misses the trip length. A stay's lodging, lodging candidates, and weather text are only in a whole read or a read of that stay, never a day read (`dayScopeLines`). At the measured density, a stay of 5 nights or more is refused too, so for such a stay they can't be read at all. Reading a stay at a time leaves both cases open, and a slimmer whole read leaves the long stay open.~~ Settled on 2026-10-26, in chat: the slimmer whole read keeps the trip-level check results, the start and end places, the dates, the rejected places, and each stay's lodging line, so they stay in reach. A stay's weather text and lodging candidates come from a read of that stay. Research doc section 5.

- ~~If a whole read gives no candidate names (version L in the research doc), how does the coordinator find which stop or stay to read when the user names a candidate in chat, such as "let's do the Desert Pearl"? For lodging, `find_place` gives the town, which points to a stay. For a meal stop, a town can hold several stops, so it would read the whole stay or try stops one at a time. A wrong guess fails quietly: `select_user_place` refuses a place that's already a candidate only on that same stop, so on another stop it adds the place as one the user named, and the stop that offered it stays undecided. The options so far: keep each undecided item's candidate names, with or without place IDs, and measure both; or a `read_itinerary` scope by place ID. Research doc section 7 says the coordinator recovers after one wasted call, since the error tells it to use `select_candidate` (tool design 2.1, `select_user_place`). That's true only when it guessed the stop or stay that offered the place.~~ Settled on 2026-10-26, in chat: a new tool searches the trip's own places by name, with string similarity, and always returns the closest few with where each sits in the trip. The whole read gives counts, not names. Research doc section 6. Still open there: whether `select_user_place` should say when the place is a candidate on another stop or stay (section 6.4).

## Do

- ~~Measure what each option saves on the 14-day trip, in characters and in tokens as the API counts them.~~ Done in the research doc, in PR #140.
- ~~Propose an answer for each open question.~~ Done, and each is settled above.
- Now that PR #140 is merged, a new session writes the design changes in research doc section 11 into the design docs, in a PR. The research doc's sections 5, 6, and 9 hold the agreed details. The same session plans the build and opens its issues. It decides how to split the build, such as whether the read change and `find_in_trip` are one issue or two. Joe asked for that decision to be made there, not in the spike.

## Done when

- Joe has agreed to an approach. Done on 2026-10-26: research doc sections 5, 6, and 9.
- The approach is written into the design docs: tool design 2.1, technical spec 5.1, 5.2, and 7.2, as research doc section 11 lists.
- The issues to build it are open.

## Ends in

A decision.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.

## Why

## Design

## What #54 found

**The trip measured.** A 14-day loop from Las Vegas with 8 stays, five stops a day, three candidates for each stop and stay, and a second set of three for about one in four of them. That's 312 candidates. It's `src/domain/fourteen-day-example.fake.ts`. Its places are made up, but each has the length of a real Google name, type, and address. Tool design 2.1 had estimated a trip like this at about 300 candidates and 20,000 tokens.

**The size of its whole read.** 72,264 characters, in 683 lines. The API counts it as 38,271 tokens for `claude-opus-5-5`, the coordinator's model. That's 1.89 characters a token. Plain English, the first 20,000 characters of DEVELOPMENT.md, came to 2.9. Tokens were counted by sending the text through the Agent SDK and taking the input tokens less those of a one-word prompt, since the plan token has no API key for the token count endpoint.

**Where the tokens go.** Measured on an earlier version of the read, at 75,613 characters:

- The 312 candidate lines were 44,832 characters and 23,183 tokens, about 60% of the read. Each gives its set, name, place ID, short line, and visit and detour times. The selected one also gives its rationale.
- Everything else was 30,800 characters and 16,177 tokens: stays, days, legs, schedules, stop lines, and check results.
- The read holds 496 IDs, such as `place_k7m2x9qa`. IDs and short lines are what make the read cost more tokens than prose.

**Scoped reads.** Each day of the trip reads at 5,202 characters at most. A stay read gives every candidate's full details, so a 3-night stay is 28,104 characters, and a 1-night stay about 12,000. A stay of 5 nights or more at this density would be refused too.

**What the tool does now.** It refuses any reply over 40,000 characters, about 21,000 tokens at 1.89, with "Can't read the itinerary: it's too large to return. Read one day, stay, or stop at a time instead." At this density, a whole read fits a trip of about a week.

**What Claude Code does over the limit.** It saves a tool result over 25,000 tokens to a file, and gives the model only the file's path and a short preview. The coordinator has no Read tool, so for it the result is cut off, with nothing to say so. 25,000 is Claude Code's default for MCP tools, and nothing in Claude Code 2.1.301, which SDK 0.3.301 ships, treats in-process servers differently.

**Every read stays in context.** A 38,000-token read at the start of each session uses that much of every later turn's input, and goes out of date with the next change.
